mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which drives corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 5%, but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and FEDFUNDS are above 4%, it indicates inflationary pressures and tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI increases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4%, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts indicate a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts are strong, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Non-farm payroll employment increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production growth signals weaker economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is below 2%, but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates during a monetary tightening cycle lead to decreased liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate is high, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
